claims.action: Commanded two thousand troops against a Turkic force of more than one hundred thousand at Zhoupan.
Served Northern Wei as regional inspector of Dingzhou.
Held the ranks of general of agile cavalry and director of the three departments with equal standing.
Brought Daxi Changru into his trusted retinue and appointed him sub-commandant.
Led Northern Zhou in the conquest of Northern Qi.
Was separately enfeoffed as a county duke.
Besieged the Chen general Wu Mingche at Luliang with Daxi Changru.
Was besieged and captured at Luliang.
Led seven thousand elite Chen troops to relieve Wu Mingche and was defeated by Daxi Changru.
Received the abdication and founded the Sui dynasty.
Raised troops in Shu against Yang Jian’s regency.
Roused six prefectures in support of Wang Qian.
Led a major Turkic invasion south in the second year of Kaihuang.
Joined Shabolue Khan’s southward invasion.
Joined Shabolue Khan’s southward invasion.
Her death caused Daxi Changru to leave office for mourning.
Raised troops against the frontier peoples under Daxi Changru’s command.
Raised troops against the frontier peoples under Daxi Changru’s command.
Raised troops against the frontier peoples under Daxi Changru’s command.
Rose to vice director of the imperial stud during the Daye reign.
Died in office in the fourteenth year of Kaihuang at age sixty.
Served Northern Wei as attendant-in-chief and grand tutor of the heir apparent.
Held the office of general of the Right Guard.
Rebelled against Yang Jian and was defeated at Ye.
Served as registrar and joined Wei Xiaokuan’s suppression of Yuchi Jiong.
Commanded the suppression of Yuchi Jiong.
Pursued Yuchi Jiong to the top of a tower with Helou Zigan.
Received the earldom of Sian when his father was promoted.
Commanded the campaign against a Tuyuhun raid on Liangzhou.
Commanded a campaign against the Turks in which Helou Zigan took a separate route.
Carried an imperial edict commending Helou Zigan.
Sent envoys offering submission and sheep and horses to Sui.
Her death caused Helou Zigan to leave office for mourning.
Succeeded Helou Zigan and rose to administrator of Qianan.
Rose to governor of three prefectures, administrator of Beidi, and duke of Dongan.
Was killed by Emperor Wen after forcefully protesting the suppression of his soldiers’ merit.
Died in the Northern Zhou conquest of Northern Qi.
Led forces against Yuchi Jiong with Shi Wansui.
Was executed for plotting rebellion; Shi Wansui was implicated through association.
Rode deep into Turkic territory with Shi Wansui to seize livestock.
Led a rebellion south of the Yangzi that Shi Wansui helped suppress.
Suppressed Shi Wansui’s victory report and falsely suggested that he had gone to the deposed crown prince.
Submitted, rebelled, bribed Shi Wansui to leave him in office, and rebelled again the next year.
A victory stele attributed to him was encountered during Shi Wansui’s southern campaign.
Reported that Shi Wansui had accepted Cuan Wan’s bribe and released him.
Succeeded Emperor Wen before Liu Fang’s Linyi campaign reached the coast.
Defended Shi Wansui’s military ability before Emperor Wen.
Joined Gao Jiong in defending Shi Wansui before Emperor Wen.
Withdrew when he learned Shi Wansui commanded the opposing Sui force.
Advanced by the Mayi route with Shi Wansui against Tardu Khan.
Served under Shi Wansui against Tardu Khan.
Served under Shi Wansui against Tardu Khan.
Served under Shi Wansui against Tardu Khan.
Was deposed as crown prince shortly before Shi Wansui’s death.
Is named as Shi Wansui’s son.
Died from illness while returning from the conquest of Linyi in the first year of Daye.
Defeated the Turks at Baidao with Liu Fang.
Seized the old city of the King of Yue, then surrendered to Liu Fang and was sent to the capital.
Is identified through his son Li Daquan, Li Fozi’s nephew.
Held Longbian for his uncle Li Fozi.
Held Wuyan as Li Fozi’s separate commander.
Served as Liu Fang’s chief clerk until grave illness forced him to remain at Yinzhou.
Helped defeat more than two thousand rebels at Dulong Ridge.
Helped defeat more than two thousand rebels at Dulong Ridge.
Helped defeat more than two thousand rebels at Dulong Ridge.
Served as Liu Fang’s chief of staff in the Linyi campaign.
Led infantry and cavalry by Yuechang in the Linyi campaign.
Led infantry and cavalry by Yuechang in the Linyi campaign.
Led infantry and cavalry by Yuechang in the Linyi campaign.
Led the fleet toward Bijing with Liu Fang and Li Gang.
Resisted Liu Fang’s invasion and abandoned the capital for the sea after defeat.
Liu Fang’s army passed his bronze frontier pillar on the way to Linyi.
Succeeded Liu Fang after his death.
Fought Turkic forces at Yifu Po and later won repeated frontier victories.
Defended the north bank of the Yangzi against Chen and served in the conquest of Chen and suppression of Gao Zhihui.
Repeatedly campaigned against the Turks and commanded Shuozhou before dying after a treason accusation.
Was captured, killed, and eaten while fighting rebels of Jiazhou after his retreat was cut off.
Repeatedly guarded the frontier and was known for charging enemy lines alone on horseback.
Repeatedly campaigned against frontier peoples and rose to commander of Xuzhou.
Joined Feng Yu in suppressing rebellious tribes.
Joined Feng Yu in suppressing rebellious tribes.
Joined Yang Wutong against the rebel Liao of Jiazhou.
The historiographer compared Shi Wansui’s character and unjust death to his.
The historiographer invoked his fame among the western Qiang.
His biography supplies the variant route name “Dingxiang route.”

offices: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry
Director of the Three Departments with Equal Standing
Valiant Grand Master of the Left Forward Army

claims.action: Served repeatedly in the vanguard, helped conquer Shu and Northern Qi, defeated Chen relief forces at Luliang, and captured Wu Mingche.
Defeated Wang Qian’s allied uprising and captured Wang Qian’s two sons.
Held a succession of northern and western commands and led an expedition beyond the Qilian Mountains.

claims.text: Known from youth for integrity and exceptional courage.
Observed mourning so severely after his mother’s death that it nearly killed him.
The historiographer praised his courage in resisting a force fifty times the size of his own.

offices: Deputy Supervisor of the New Capital

claims.action: Helped suppress Yuchi Jiong and was first over the wall in repeated battles.
Defeated Tuyuhun and Turkic forces, using control of water to exhaust the enemy at Mount Keluoqi.
Proposed replacing vulnerable distant military farms with linked garrisons, beacon towers, and guarded routes; Emperor Wen accepted the proposal.

claims.summary: Memorial on practical defense of Longxi and the lands west of the Yellow River.

claims.derivation: East Asian age sixty at death in AD 594

claims.text: Known from youth for martial daring and praised as forceful and capable.
The historiographer praised the security he brought to the western and northern frontiers.

claims.derivation: Age fifteen at the AD 564 battle of Mount Mang

offices: Director of the Bureau with Equal Standing
Director with Equal Standing of the First Rank

claims.action: Rallied faltering troops before Ye and helped defeat Yuchi Jiong.
After penal assignment to Dunhuang, proved his mounted-archery skill, raided Turkic territory, and won a single-combat challenge for Dou Rongding.
Fought more than seven hundred engagements suppressing Gao Zhihui’s southern rebellion and sent a report in a bamboo tube when cut off.
Defeated more than thirty communities in the south but accepted Cuan Wan’s bribe and left him in office.
Pursued and defeated Tardu Khan’s withdrawing army, but Yang Su suppressed the victory.

actions: stripped of rank and assigned to Dunhuang

claims.summary: Denied accepting Cuan Wan’s bribe and explained why he had left him in office.

claims.text: Did not impose rigid camp order, adapted freely in battle, and was regarded as a fine general.
The historiographer praised his courage, care for soldiers, and far-reaching victories, and judged that he died for no true crime.

offices: Senior Attendant of the Imperial Carriage
Director with Equal Standing of the First Rank

claims.action: Helped defeat Yuchi Jiong and later fought the Turks at Baidao.
Led twenty-seven battalions against Li Fozi, combined severe discipline with care for sick soldiers, and secured his surrender.
Defeated Linyi’s forces, entered its capital, and returned after recording the victory in stone.

claims.circumstance: died of illness returning from Linyi

claims.text: Contemporaries regarded him as a fine general for combining authority and kindness.
The historiographer praised his impartial orders, strict command, and conquest of Linyi.

offices: Pillar of State of the First Rank
General of the Left Martial Guard

claims.text: Known for stratagems, martial skill, and repeated frontier victories.
Known for fierce courage, archery, and command talent.
Known for bold spirit, strategy, and a frontier reputation feared by the Turks.
Known for resolute courage and mounted archery.
Known for fierce courage and for charging enemy formations alone.
Known for firmness and military strategy.
